Captures the PM's verbatim intent, the Shape-Up-style appetite BUDGET, a coarse provisional t-shirt routing estimate, and which room (dispatch/shape/plan/roadmap) the work should enter. intent.description: The PM ask, verbatim. Not paraphrased or summarized — the raw framing the sizing lobby routed on.

appetite.description: The Shape-Up BUDGET the PM MAY state for this work — never collected before the size is delivered, and never a precondition for this sizing-object to validate (see `required`, which does not name this field). Its absence is a legitimate state meaning 'not yet asked, or not volunteered'; it is recorded once the PM has answered the open post-size prompt. When the PM does state one, it is a FIXED BUDGET, NOT a reason to defer scope and NOT 'appetite-based OOS' (which coordinator doctrine bans — see coordinator/docs/wiki/implementation-standards-by-domain.md § Cross-cutting standards: 'OOS framing must be architectural, not appetite-based'). Appetite bounds how much time/effort is worth spending; it never justifies cutting a correctness/integrity requirement out of scope. INDEPENDENT OF estimate.tshirt: appetite is the PM's budget, the estimate is the EM's read of engineering complexity, and neither is an input to the other. On the default path that independence is now STRUCTURAL — there is no appetite in hand when the estimate is set — and it still holds on the volunteered path: a large appetite is not evidence the work is large; a small one never shrinks the read.

estimate.description: Coarse routing-only size estimate. Distinct from the committed plan-body LoE (two-altitude model, D1.3): this estimate exists to pick which room (route) the work enters, not to bind the eventual plan's effort accounting.

tshirt.description: T-shirt size estimate. Reuses the existing loe.tshirt enum and weights verbatim (XS=1, S=2, M=4, L=8, XL=16) — see coordinator/schemas/completion-entry.schema.json loe.tshirt. Do not invent a parallel scale. `XXL` is the sixth notch and is ROUTING-ALTITUDE ONLY: it names an ask whose PLAN ITSELF exceeds one window, and it resolves directly to the `goal-setting` room rather than to any XL exit. It is ALSO a real notch on the effort ladder (coordinator/config/loe-thresholds.yaml), not vocabulary borrowed one-way into `loe.tshirt`: `chain_loe.tshirt` carries it too, because a chain's summed dispatches/tokens reach it routinely even though one session rarely does. An earlier revision of this sentence claimed XXL was never valid as a completed-work level of effort and that `chain_loe.tshirt` stayed XS–XL for that reason; that was retracted at completion-entry 1.4.0 — it described a ladder that saturated at XL rather than one that had been deliberately capped. Set from engineering complexity ALONE — surfaces touched, proven-vs-novel pattern, number of independent pieces. On the default path there is no appetite to anchor to, because none is collected before the size is delivered; where the PM has volunteered one unprompted, it is still not an input, and a t-shirt landing on the same notch as that volunteered budget is the anchoring tell, not a size.

provisional.description: Always true. Marks this tshirt value as a COARSE, revisable ROUTING estimate (which room to enter) — never the committed plan-body LoE. A plan authored downstream re-estimates independently; this field is not inherited as authoritative effort.

route.description: The room this sizing routes the work into: dispatch=small enough to execute directly, no artifact; spec-dispatch=small enough for a light plan artifact then dispatch, no Opus plan review; shape=problem not yet converged, needs /shape first; plan=decision-weight work needing coordinator:plan; roadmap=initiative-scale, needs roadmap-planning; pm-decision=initiative-scale and not a room by itself — the engine picks no room and the PM chooses among the offered exits (see `xl_exit`); goal-setting=the XXL room, needing coordinator:goal-setting to produce ratified OKRs plus roadmap-seed stubs. `goal-setting` is a resolved room, not a fifth XL exit — XL has four exits and is therefore a PM decision, XXL has exactly one room and is therefore a determinate map. detents.description: Boundary detents crossed or acknowledged while sizing this work — the discrete stops the sizing lobby snapped to (e.g. appetite/estimate divergence, route-boundary crossing) before landing on the final route. Empty array when no boundary was crossed. `premise_unproven` and `premise_not_applicable` are ADVISORY: they mirror the `premise.provenance` value (see the `premise` object) into a queryable detent, but never change the resolved `route` and never populate `xl_exit`. `post_size_prompt_pending` is the POSITIVE, engine-emitted signal that the size has been delivered at M/L/XL with no appetite recorded and the EM is waiting on the PM's open post-size answer — it is what every downstream consumer keys the open-halt exemption on. NEVER infer that halt from `appetite`'s absence instead: absence is the shape every M+ record carries by construction, whether or not a size was ever delivered or a question ever asked. `xxl_unprobed` and `goal_setting_pm_gated` are likewise ADVISORY, never blocking. `xxl_unprobed` fires when an XXL resolved with NO recorded `scout_evidence` — it watches the absence of EVIDENCE, not the absence of a PROBE, because the engine observes only the probe string and never whether one was justified; that predicate covers both reachable cells, the XL→XXL probe-raised promotion and the no-op raise clamped at the ladder top. `goal_setting_pm_gated` records that this sizing landed in a room the EM cannot enter without a PM utterance, closing a monotonicity inversion in which an XL carried a queryable 'a PM must speak' marker (`pm_decision_pending`) while a strictly larger XXL carried none. `boundary_counted_in_notch` and `scout_evidence_mention_count` are ADVISORY on the same terms: the first fires when a cross-repo boundary/memo/relay/assent gate contributed to the notch (a memo is a GATE, not a size — only negotiated co-design earns the notch), the second when the scout evidence behind the size is a mention-count rather than a change-set. Unlike the premise pair, `boundary_counted_in_notch` is NOT size-gated — the size is the thing a counted boundary is suspected of having inflated, so gating on it would exempt the reads the detent exists to catch. `intent_em_elaborated` and `precedent_shipped_before` are ADVISORY on those same terms: the first fires when the recorded `intent` is the EM's restatement rather than the PM's own words (`--intent-source em-elaborated`), the second when the ask repeats an operation whose runbook exists and has already landed (`--precedent shipped-before`) — a repeat is dispatch-shaped by default, but never auto-collapsed, because a repeat can genuinely be larger and the engine cannot see which. Neither is size-gated, for `boundary_counted_in_notch`'s reason: the size is what an elaborated intent is suspected of having inflated. `probe_raise_on_substrate_condition` is the ONE value in this array that is not advisory — it records that a Step 2 probe `raise` declared `--probe-raise-basis substrate-condition` was NOT applied, leaving the notch where the gut-read put it. That suppression is a READ discriminator, not an unread one: the caller applied the discriminator by choosing the value, and an area's health is not a size signal by definition. The route still resolves from the t-shirt→route table, so the Hard Gate holds — the SIZE moved, the route did not get overridden. An EM whose ask genuinely grew answers `ask-scope`, keeps the raise, and has made a recorded falsifiable assertion — recorded as `probe_raise_ask_scope_asserted`, which is ADVISORY and fires when a probe `raise` declared `--probe-raise-basis ask-scope` was APPLIED. It changes nothing: the raise has already moved the notch, and its only job is to make the assertion findable, so that both answers to the basis question leave a queryable mark and only one costs the raise. It fires ONLY on an actual `raise` — an `ask-scope` basis passed with no raise, or alongside a `collapse`, describes a resize that never happened, and marking it would put noise in exactly the field a later reader queries for signal. `probe_raise_on_breadth` is the SECOND non-advisory value, on identical terms to `probe_raise_on_substrate_condition`: it records that a Step 2 probe `raise` declared `--probe-raise-basis breadth` was NOT applied. A probe that found more sites than the gut-read saw, each taking the same edit and none touching another, found more of the SAME ask rather than a bigger one — breadth is a dispatch shape, not a notch, and the count belongs in the dispatch plan. The discriminator the caller applies by choosing this value is uniformity: sites that each need their own call, or that interact, are depth wearing a count and answer `ask-scope` instead.

fork.description: Null unless appetite and estimate diverge (estimate's implied size exceeds or undershoots the appetite budget). When set, this is UNRESOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION — the sizing skill surfaces the fork to the PM, it never auto-resolves it. cut_to_fit=trim scope to fit the existing appetite; raise_appetite=the PM increases the budget instead.

xl_exit.description: The PM's recorded choice among the XL exits when `route` is `pm-decision`. The engine NEVER sets this — it always emits `null`, exactly as it does for `fork`. `null` is a legitimate open state meaning the PM has not chosen yet; it NEVER means the multi-session exit was accepted by default. Three exits are CURRENTLY OFFERED, each with a stated precondition: shape=the job-to-be-done is not stated, or the EM cannot falsifiably restate the problem in the PM's vocabulary; roadmap=the work spans >=2 named workstreams, or carries (or needs) an initiative/goal FK — a programme of plans, not one plan; accept_multi_session=none of the other preconditions hold and the PM has explicitly assented — writing this value IS that record. The fourth value, split, is RETAINED AS LEGACY VOCABULARY ONLY: it is not an offered exit and must not be re-offered (see this schema's `x-bump-note` for when and why it was withdrawn) — it remains a valid enum value solely so existing records that already carry it continue to validate (precondition history: docs/wiki/sizing-lobby.md § pm-decision). An ask that decomposes into independently shippable pieces routes to roadmap.

scout_evidence.description: Pointers to cartography/scout output that informed this sizing (file paths, wiki citations, prior-art references). Empty array when no scout ran. Each item is EITHER a bare string pointer OR a structured object (`kind`, `finding`, optional `note`) when the pointer needs per-item annotation. NEGATIVE SPEC, load-bearing: the per-item `kind` here is NEVER the same home as `probe.scout_evidence_kind` below and never overrides it — `probe.scout_evidence_kind` is the SIZING-LEVEL answer, the one value the assembler actually consumed at Step 3, mirroring the single `--scout-evidence-kind` flag; a per-item `kind` is finer-grained annotation on one piece of evidence, not a competing sizing-level signal.

kind.description: Same vocabulary as `probe.scout_evidence_kind` (mention-count|change-set|site-count), but scoped to this ONE evidence item — never a substitute for the sizing-level `probe.scout_evidence_kind`.

finding.description: The evidence itself, stated so a reader who was not in the session can act on it.

surfaced_to_pm.description: Direction-class items the sizing surfaced to the PM but deliberately did NOT decide. Distinct from `fork` and `xl_exit`, which are the two structured halts the lobby computes for itself: this array is for everything else the EM noticed while sizing that is the PM's call — a standing ruling the new evidence bears on, a product-direction question the work would force, an external-facing consequence. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is never a record of a decision. An entry stays listed until it is resolved in its own artifact (a decision record, a PM ruling, a downstream plan); resolving it by editing the sizing-object is the failure this field exists to prevent. Once resolved, the PM's reasoning moves to `pm_resolution`. Empty array when nothing was surfaced. Exists because the alternative — a YAML comment — is invisible to any query over state/sizings/, which is how a surfaced item silently becomes a forgotten one.

item.description: The direction-class question itself, stated so a reader who was not in the session can act on it. Not a topic label.

why_not_decided.description: Why the EM did not settle this while sizing — e.g. a standing PM ruling this evidence bears on but does not overturn, product direction, an irreversible/external action, or a genuine no-correct-answer tradeoff. 'Not now' is not a reason; if the only reason is cost, it is break-class work to be fixed, not a direction-class item to be surfaced.

prior_ruling.description: Optional pointer to the existing decision, ruling, or audit entry this item bears on (file:line, DR-id, or artifact path). Present when the item revisits settled ground rather than opening new ground — its absence means no prior ruling was found, not that none exists.

pm_resolution.description: The PM's recorded answer once they have resolved this sizing's open questions — the counterpart to `surfaced_to_pm`, which holds what is still open. Free-form string values by design: what a PM settles at a sizing varies (which fork, which XL exit, where an artifact should live), and a closed property list would push the next unanticipated decision back into an ad-hoc key or a comment. NEGATIVE SPEC: `fork` and `xl_exit` remain the AUTHORITATIVE machine-readable record of those two choices — an entry here carries the PM's REASONING, never a substitute value, and must not contradict them. Omit entirely when nothing has been resolved; an empty object is not a resolution.

decided_on.description: Date the PM actually decided (YYYY-MM-DD), not the date the sizing was authored.

additionalProperties.description: One resolved question, keyed by what it resolved (e.g. `post_size_prompt`, `xl_exit`, `wiki_home`). Value states the choice AND the reasoning, so a later reader need not reconstruct why.

status.description: Sizing-object lifecycle. draft=intent captured, not yet estimated; sized=estimate+appetite set, fork may be outstanding; routed=route chosen and handed off (fork, if any, resolved); superseded=replaced by a later sizing for the same intent; shipped=terminal — the downstream work this sizing routed into has shipped; declined=terminal — routed, then the spend was refused on direction-class grounds. declined is NOT superseded: the sizing was sound and has no successor, nothing invalidated it, `superseded_note`'s 'verification that invalidated it' does not apply. declined is NOT shipped: nothing landed. Always paired with a decision-record backlink recording why.

deliverable_id.description: Durable deliverable join key. Minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact — a sizing-object is now the earliest artifact in the deliverable chain, so this is where the key is first minted. Null for pre-backfill records. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-08-08-sizing-objects-join-the-deliverable-spine.md § C2.

plan.description: FK to the plan (docs/plans/<name>.md) this sizing-object routed into. Optional and nullable. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is never a substitute for `deliverable_id` — `plan` is the human-readable pointer to one downstream artifact, `deliverable_id` is the spine key that actually joins the chain. Mirrors plan.schema.json's own `sizing_object` field by symmetry (that field points a plan back at its originating sizing-object; this one points forward at the plan it routed into). Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-08-08-sizing-objects-join-the-deliverable-spine.md § C2.

superseded_note.description: Present only when `status` is `superseded`. Records WHY this sizing-object was superseded — the verification that invalidated it, the root cause, and where the live surface moved to. Distinct from `pm_resolution`: this is EM-observed process history about the sizing-object's own lifecycle, not the PM's decision reasoning, and must not be folded into `pm_resolution`.

premise.description: Whether the premise this sizing is built on was ever actually verified, before structure gets built on top of a guess. ADVISORY ONLY — the detent this can produce downstream (`sizing_assemble`'s `premise_unproven`, engine-side) NEVER blocks a route; it never changes the resolved `route` and never populates `xl_exit`. Discharge is by CITING THE EXECUTED EVIDENCE INLINE in the `evidence` field below — a file:line, test name, command output, or read location the author actually looked at — NEVER by producing a separate spike-result record; a premise question is answered in place, not spun into its own artifact. `provenance`: executed=the premise was verified by actually running/reproducing it; read=the premise rests on reading code/docs/a prior record, not on execution; not-applicable=this ask has no premise to verify (state the reason in `evidence`); unrecorded=migration-only, meaning this record predates this field and its premise provenance was never captured. DR-068 (docs/decisions/DR-068-commit-time-coverage-gate-scoped-shift-left-ambient-handoff-flat-fallback-advisory.md) is the standing precedent for this advisory-not-blocking shape — that ruling made the same call for the commit-time DAG verdict, and this field follows the same house answer rather than inventing a new one.

provenance.description: executed=verified by actually running/reproducing it; read=rests on reading code/docs/a prior record, not execution; not-applicable=this ask has no premise to verify; unrecorded=migration-only, the record predates this field.

evidence.description: The executed evidence cited inline (file:line, test name, command output, or read location) — or, when `provenance` is `not-applicable`, why. Required for every `provenance` value except `unrecorded`.

spike_verdict.description: Path to the spike-verdict record produced by `coordinator:spike` when a spike upgraded this sizing's premise from `read` to `executed`. NEGATIVE SPEC: never substitutes for `evidence` — `evidence` stays required for every provenance value except `unrecorded`, and the inline citation remains the discharge (see this object's own "answered in place, not spun into its own artifact" rule). `spike_verdict` is the structured pointer to the ceremony record; `evidence` is still what a reader reads. Absent when no spike ran.

spike_amendments.description: BINDING SCOPE for the downstream plan — the discharged routing intent a `coordinator:spike` produced, recorded where the plan-author will read it. NEGATIVE SPEC: not a substitute for the downstream plan's own scope or chunking, and not a place to record spike findings that changed nothing — an entry exists because it re-specs something. Omit entirely when no spike ran; an empty array is not an amendment set.

scope.description: What this amendment binds: the named sub-piece of the ask it re-specs, or `cross-cutting` for one that binds the whole. Always a string, even when the underlying identifier is numeric.

amendment.description: The binding routing intent the spike produced for this scope: what the spike's executed evidence changed about how this work must be planned.

intent_source.description: Whether `intent` above is the PM's own sentence or the EM's restatement — the `--intent-source` flag `coordinator/skills/sizing/SKILL.md` § Step 3 instructs the EM to pass to `sizing-assemble`. pm-verbatim=these are the PM's words, unedited. em-elaborated=`intent` is the EM's own three-clause elaboration rather than a quote, declared rather than smoothed to look verbatim — the skill names editing a restatement to LOOK verbatim as the exact failure this field exists to catch. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is the RAW INPUT, distinct from the `detents` value `intent_em_elaborated`, which is the assembler's COMPUTED audit-trail record that this input was `em-elaborated`; `pm-verbatim` records as that detent's absence, not as a value here. Optional because express-lane sizings skip Step 3 entirely.

precedent.description: Whether this fleet has run this operation before with a runbook that already landed — the `--precedent` flag from SKILL.md § Step 3. shipped-before=a repeat, dispatch-shaped by default; novel=no prior runbook. NEGATIVE SPEC: `shipped-before` is advisory input, never a collapse — a repeat CAN genuinely be larger, and neither the skill nor the engine can see which, so this field records the claim without resizing anything. Distinct from `detents`' `precedent_shipped_before`, which is the assembler's computed record that this value fired; `novel` records as that detent's absence. Optional because express-lane sizings skip Step 3 entirely.

boundary_in_notch.description: The EM's answer to § A cross-team dependency is a gate, not a size: did a cross-repo boundary, memo, relay, or assent gate contribute to this sizing's notch? The `--boundary-in-notch` flag SKILL.md § Step 3 names as 'what makes [the discriminator] checkable' — a memo is a GATE, not a size, and only negotiated co-design earns the notch. Always present on every non-express-lane sizing per the skill. NEGATIVE SPEC: distinct from `detents`' `boundary_counted_in_notch`, which is the assembler's computed record that `yes` fired; `no` records as that detent's absence. This field is NOT size-gated for the same reason its detent counterpart is not: the size is precisely the value a counted boundary is suspected of having inflated, so gating the check on that size would exempt the reads it exists to catch. WHY THIS ACCEPTS A BOOLEAN AND THE OTHER THREE FLAG-MIRRORS DO NOT — a YAML 1.1 TRAP, found live while backfilling the first record to carry this field: the CLI vocabulary is `yes|no`, and a sizing-object is YAML, where an UNQUOTED `no` parses as boolean `false`, not the string `"no"`. A string-only enum would therefore reject the spelling the skill tells the EM to write, on the majority path, and the failure reads as a schema bug rather than a quoting one. Both spellings validate and mean the same thing; `"yes"`/`true` are the positive arm. `intent_source`, `precedent`, and `probe.*` need no such arm — none of their values is a YAML boolean literal.

probe.description: The Step 2 substrate probe's outcome, when one ran — the `--probe-signal`/`--probe-raise-basis`/`--scout-evidence-kind` flags SKILL.md § Step 3 passes to `sizing-assemble`. Omit entirely when no probe ran (the skill allows an express-lane or confident XS/S read to skip Step 2 with no probe); an empty object is not a no-op probe.

signal.description: collapse=the probe found the ask smaller than the gut-read (an over-read); raise=the probe found the ask bigger (an under-read). `raise_basis` is only meaningful alongside `raise` — a `collapse` probe, or one with no basis at all, never carries it, and a basis paired with `collapse` describes a resize that never happened.

raise_basis.description: Why a `raise` moved the notch — required to be meaningful only when `signal` is `raise`. ask-scope=the probe found the request itself reaches further than the gut-read saw; this basis KEEPS the raise and fires the advisory `probe_raise_ask_scope_asserted`. substrate-condition=the probe found the ground underneath in poor repair, not the request bigger — a finding about the AREA, not the ASK, same shape as § A cross-team dependency is a gate, not a size; this basis is NOT APPLIED, the notch stays put, and `probe_raise_on_substrate_condition` records the suppression. breadth=the probe found more sites than expected but all alike, uniform, disjoint, and taking the same edit — more of the SAME ask, not a bigger one, so the width goes to the dispatch plan, not the notch; NOT APPLIED, and `probe_raise_on_breadth` records the suppression. The route still resolves from the t-shirt->route table on either suppressed basis, so § Hard gate is untouched.

scout_evidence_kind.description: What kind of evidence backs a `scout_evidence` entry from Step 2 — repeatable per finding at the flag level, recorded once here at the sizing level for the class. mention-count=a grep/reference count, which is NOT a change-set until someone has asked what a compatibility layer absorbs; fires the advisory `scout_evidence_mention_count` rather than being read as raw engineering complexity. change-set=files that actually change. site-count=call/usage sites. `change-set` and `site-count` fire nothing on `detents` — they are answers that describe evidence already qualified as to WHAT was counted, and say nothing about depth on their own.

detent_discharges.description: Per-detent discharge for an advisory that says 'discharge by naming what is specifically different this time' — keyed by the detent name as it appears in `detents[]`, valued by the EM's written discharge for it. Optional and never a precondition for this sizing-object to validate (see `required`, which does not name this field): its absence is legitimate, meaning no detent has been discharged here yet, exactly as `appetite`'s absence means 'not yet asked, or not volunteered'. NEGATIVE SPEC: never a substitute for `surfaced_to_pm`, which holds direction-class items the EM deliberately did NOT decide — a discharge here is the EM's own engineering judgment, settled in place, not a PM-owned open question forwarded for a ruling.

additionalProperties.description: The EM's written discharge for the keyed detent — what is specifically different this time, stated so a reader who was not in the session can act on it.
